subject: Reserved pool allocation instability — update & next steps

Subject: Re: Strange 503s and high tail latency on reserved pool

Hi Mina,

We're seeing ~15-30% of requests to our reserved GPU pool start returning 503s and 5–10s tail latency spikes starting ~01:45 PDT this morning. These are intermittent but correlate with our peak batch window and are causing downstream order enrichment jobs to backlog.

Attached are a small sample of request IDs and one log bundle from our side. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side (allocator or autoscaler) or something we should change in our client config? We have a scheduled nighttime batch at 03:00 PDT and we'd like to avoid further failures.

Request sample: BR-req-9812, BR-req-9817, BR-req-9829
Impact: high - batch latency causing missed SLAs to internal downstream systems

Thanks,
Tamara

We’ll confirm the mitigation within 20–30 minutes. I’ll provide a timeline and a short incident timeline once we have a root-cause hypothesis.

Subject: Re: Strange 503s and high tail latency on reserved pool (allocator snapshot)

Capturing quick notes from the allocator snapshot we pulled at 02:35 PDT:
- Observed allocator starvation on pool-rsv-74: a small set of long-running KV cache warmups are holding GPU slots in PENDING state while new allocations queue.
- Autoscaler incorrectly interpreted queued allocations as capacity pressure and attempted scale-out. Scale-out failed due to a transient image pull error in the warm node group (ECR throttling); that left queued allocations unresolved.
- Fallback routing was configured but threshold was conservative (10% queue length) and wasn't triggered before latency hit customer-visible levels.

Immediate remediation applied (@02:45 PDT):
- Increased soft concurrency for pool-rsv-74 by 25% to allow immediate headroom.
- Disabled warmup-affinity for long-running KV cache workers to release the slots faster.
- Manually launched two warm standby nodes with a pre-pulled image to avoid the ECR pull race.

I attached the allocator snapshot and a minimal timeline. We should follow up with:
1) Autoscaler fix to not treat queued-but-warmup allocations as unmet capacity.
2) ECR pull retry/backoff improvements for warm node group.
3) Lower fallback threshold for customer-facing reserved pools.

Ben
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: allocator-snapshot-20280319.tar.gz, incident-timeline.csv

Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 03:05:00 -0700
Subject: Status update: mitigation applied and monitoring

Tamara — quick update: we implemented the mitigations Ben listed at 02:45 PDT. Early results: error rates have fallen back to baseline and tail latency is trending down. We have not seen repeat 5–10s spikes in the last 15 minutes.

What we did for BrightRetail in the short term:
- 25% soft concurrency increase on your reserved pool (non-disruptive).
- Disabled warmup-affinity for long KV cache workers to avoid slot hogging.
- Brought up 2 pre-warmed nodes with pre-pulled images to bypass ECR pull issues.

Next steps and timeline:
- We will monitor for 6 hours and keep your team informed every 60 minutes.
- Our postmortem draft (internal) will be shared within 72 hours, and we’ll include a customer-facing summary and any credits/SLAs we will apply.
- Engineering follow-ups: autoscaler affinity logic change (ETA ~2 weeks), fallback threshold adjustment (ETA ~3 days), ECR retry/backoff patch (ETA ~1 week).

If you see anything unexpected please ping me directly (urgent channel) and we’ll escalate. We’ll also follow-up with a brief post-incident meeting — propose Wed 10:00 PDT for a 20-minute sync; you can decline if you prefer written notes.

Thanks for the quick report and patience — we’ll get you a formal timeline + remediation plan in the next 72 hours.

— Mina

Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: allocator starvation on reserved pool (BrightRetail)

Tamara — thanks again for your patience while we worked through the incident. This is a short customer-facing summary; I’ve attached the internal postmortem draft and the incident timeline CSV for your reference.

Summary (impact):
- Window: 2028-03-19 01:45–03:00 PDT (intermittent).
- Effect: 15–30% elevated request error rates (503) and 5–10s tail latency spikes affecting batch jobs.
- Root cause (high level): allocator starvation combined with an autoscaler decision path that attempted scale-out while warm node provisioning hit transient ECR pull failures. Some long-running KV-cache warmups held GPU slots in PENDING state and prevented rapid turnover.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Increased soft concurrency and disabled warmup-affinity for the affected pool.
- Manually launched pre-warmed nodes with pre-pulled images to avoid the ECR pull race.
- Temporarily lowered the fallback routing threshold for reserved pools (short-term rollback after monitoring).

Planned follow-ups (customer-impacting items prioritized):
1) Autoscaler logic change to ignore warmup-occupied slots for capacity decisions (ETA: 2 weeks).
2) ECR pull backoff & warm node-group pre-pull improvement (ETA: 1 week).
3) Fallback threshold tuning for high-SLA reserved pools (ETA: 3 days).
4) Customer runbook update: we will add guidance for optional client-side retry window tuning for large batch jobs (ETA: 1 week).

Credits and next steps:
- We will provide a billing credit for the impacted window equivalent to 20% of charges for the reserved pool on 2028-03-19; our finance team will reach out to confirm amounts and booking.
- Please review the attached postmortem draft and let us know any sensitive details you prefer redacted before we publish a final customer-facing version.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx, incident-timeline.csv
Link to internal postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/brightretail/incident-20280319

Proposed short review call: Fri 2028-03-24 10:00 PDT (20 minutes). If that works I’ll send an invite.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take incidents like this seriously and are prioritizing fixes that avoid recurrence.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
